nodes.label: Adopt Connections With accept(), Never available()
nodes.rationale: accept() hands over a connection exactly once, transferring ownership. available() returns whichever client has unread data and returns that same client again on every call, so an accept loop built on it adopts one connection into several slots and splits one HTTP request across several sockets.
nodes.community_name: Adopt Connections With accept(), Never available
nodes.norm_label: adopt connections with accept(), never available()

nodes.label: Detect Disconnects Before Accepting
nodes.rationale: Order inside Poll() matters: disconnect detection, then accept, then pump. If accept runs first a just-dropped slot can be handed to a new connection before net_close is sent, and the Linux side feeds new bytes into the old socket.

nodes.label: Edge-Triggered was_up Disconnect Tracking
nodes.rationale: Act on the was-connected to not-connected transition. Testing !connected() every pass emits net_close continuously for slots that are merely idle.

nodes.label: loop() Must Yield
nodes.rationale: Poll() returns immediately when idle so loop() spins at full speed, starving the Bridge RPC thread until servo_read misses its 10s deadline. A delay(1) at the end of Tick() costs nothing against the latency budget.

nodes.label: One Bulk Read Per Slot Per Pass
nodes.rationale: Use client.read(buffer, sizeof(buffer)), not a byte-at-a-time loop, and never block or delay() inside the pump because the same loop() also drives the servo bus.
nodes.norm_label: one bulk read per slot per pass

nodes.label: kRelayChunkBytes Must Match relay_chunk_bytes
nodes.rationale: One number in two places, bytes per Bridge message. Halving it doubles the number of Bridge round trips for identical payload; 256 is the value the working relay used.

nodes.label: Bridge Net Contract
nodes.rationale: MCU to Linux: net_open(slot, client_ip), net_rx(slot, data), net_close(slot). Linux to MCU: net_tx(slot, data), net_shutdown(slot).

nodes.label: provide_safe Registration
nodes.rationale: net_tx and net_shutdown are called from the Bridge thread while loop() may be inside the relay, so they must be registered with provide_safe. Payloads are MsgPack bin_t and must not be packed into a String.

nodes.label: Serial Works; Monitor Is Optional
nodes.rationale: The sketch prints through Serial and that is proven. Monitor (the Bridge console facade) only adds reach to App Lab over WiFi; there is no correctness reason to switch.

nodes.label: Rewriting Instead Of Porting Reintroduced Solved Bugs
nodes.rationale: The relay was once rewritten from scratch instead of ported, and the rewrite reintroduced problems the original had already solved. The reference is the Stage-2 relay sketch.

nodes.label: Count

nodes.label: Output degree

nodes.rationale: A saved, named position an operator captures and can re-select. The genus; the datum is one distinguished member. Avoid preset, bookmark, waypoint, favourite.

nodes.rationale: The one absolute zero reference, captured by Calibrate from a validated reading at the documented physical reference position. Exactly one, cannot be deleted, must sit mid-travel — a datum at count 0 strands the negative half of the window. Avoid zero point, home, origin, offset.

nodes.label: Baseline
nodes.rationale: The position of the currently active zero reference — the point output degrees are measured from. Activating another zero moves the baseline without disturbing the datum.

nodes.label: Travel window
nodes.rationale: The reachable output-angle range, plus/minus 90 degrees by default. A target outside it is refused as out_of_travel, never clamped.

nodes.label: Snapshot
nodes.rationale: One instantaneous sensory readout from the servo carrying its own valid flag. An invalid snapshot is a failed read, not a reading of zero.

nodes.label: Sample
nodes.rationale: One persisted telemetry row written by the sampler at the configured interval and subject to retention. Distinct from a snapshot.

nodes.label: Fault

nodes.rationale: _position_verified is False after every boot and the UI says so, yet the backend accepts move commands deliberately. The safety-shaped intuition to refuse them is wrong here for operational rather than technical reasons.

nodes.label: Remote site makes refusal less safe, not more
nodes.rationale: Access is a three-hour drive. If the measured signal is lost the operator must recover it without dispatching anyone, and may need to drive to an externally held reference. Refusing movement until someone physically presses Calibrate converts a recoverable situation into a site visit; a system that locks itself out of the only remedy available to a remote operator is less safe. Consequences: the unverified warning in app.js is load-bearing, travel-window enforcement remains the real guard, and D1 must be fixed by making the datum trustworthy rather than by gating movement.

nodes.label: ADR inclusion criteria
nodes.rationale: A decision gets an ADR only if it is hard to reverse, surprising without context, and the result of a real trade-off. Failing any of the three means no ADR. Do not re-litigate: amend or supersede explicitly rather than quietly building against one.

nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md routes; CONTEXT.md is glossary only with no status, decisions or layout; CONVENTIONS.md holds style including undecided items; docs/ holds state, backlog, ADRs, the frozen audit and the file registry.

nodes.label: Four easily conflated position terms
nodes.rationale: Zero reference (the genus), datum (the one absolute member), baseline (whichever is active), and the servo's kLock EEPROM write-lock register which is not the Lock.

nodes.label: Open work lives only in docs/BACKLOG.md
nodes.rationale: There is no external issue tracker; the gh-based workflow once described here was never used and has been removed.

nodes.label: Why the code lives in src/
nodes.rationale: Arduino compiles src/ recursively and does no preprocessing on .cpp/.h; only .ino files get concatenated and prototypes generated. Putting logic in src/ yields ordinary reviewable C++ with real headers, namespaces and classes and no compiler magic, leaving sketch.ino as four lines handing off to App. .h files in a sketch are not auto-included, which is why every file declares its own includes.

nodes.label: Sketch class responsibilities
nodes.rationale: AngleConverter (counts <-> output degrees, direction sign), SignMagnitude (STS wire-format decode, the 'reads 32700' bug), ServoFaults (status 0x41 to six named flags), ServoBus (the only place touching the serial bus: retries, EEPROM unlock ritual), ServoController (the operations the backend asks for), SpiRemap (routes SPI2 to ICSP), NetworkRelay (shield <-> Linux byte pump, callback seam, no Bridge dependency), BridgeApi (the contract with Python, the only file knowing payload formats), App (composition root).

nodes.label: Header-only Arduino-free classes enable host tests
nodes.rationale: AngleConverter, SignMagnitude and ServoFaults are header-only and Arduino-free on purpose — that is what makes them testable on a development machine with plain g++.

nodes.label: Two test tiers: host-native and on-target
nodes.rationale: They catch different things. Host-native runs constantly in milliseconds with no board, covering sign-magnitude decoding, angle round-trips within one count, the +/-90 window fitting one servo turn, direction mirroring, speed conversion and every status bit. On-target covers only what a host cannot: that the servo answers, configuration writes stick, a commanded move lands, and stop holds. OnTarget is not compiled into the main sketch because recursive compilation is limited to src/.
nodes.norm_label: two test tiers: host-native and on-target

nodes.label: TinyTest.h instead of AUnit or GoogleTest
nodes.rationale: A ~60-line harness, deliberately not a third-party framework: every dependency is a liability on an air-gapped machine.
nodes.norm_label: tinytest.h instead of aunit or googletest

nodes.label: Apply SpiRemap twice
nodes.rationale: The UNO Q routes SPI2 to D11-D13 but the Ethernet Shield takes SPI from the ICSP header (PD1/PC2/PC3). Ethernet.init() re-initialises the SPI pins and undoes the first remap, so it must be applied again afterwards or the W5500 reports 'no hardware'.

nodes.label: Drain with while, never if
nodes.rationale: The UART RX ring is 64 bytes and the socket buffers are small; one byte per loop() is not fast enough.

nodes.label: The Bridge payload contract with Python
nodes.rationale: servo_read -> snapshot CSV; servo_move 'counts,speed,accel'; servo_stop; servo_set_deadband 'counts'; servo_configure_range 'multiturn,amplification'; servo_centre_here; get_status -> 'ready' | 'no-servo'. Snapshot fields: valid,counts,moving,temp_c,volt_v,curr_a,torque_kgcm,load,status_bits. Plain comma-separated payloads are readable in a log and neither side can drift from a field order the other assumes.
